key_insight: Trials that require English proficiency enroll fewer Asian and Hispanic/Latinx participants, while language accommodation remains uncommon.
clinical_relevance: Reviewing and revising language eligibility criteria could be a practical way to improve trial diversity and better reflect the populations affected by cancer and other diseases.
method: Cross-sectional analysis of ClinicalTrials.gov interventional trials with at least one US site and posted results.
Eligibility criteria were parsed with validated regular expressions to identify English-language requirements and language accommodations.
Enrolled race and ethnicity composition was analyzed with adjusted generalized linear models across 44,487 trials.
evidence_signal: Among exclusively US-site trials, 12.9% included an English-language requirement and 1.8% documented language accommodation; the classifier showed 88.2% sensitivity and 99.2% specificity.
watch_item: Associations are observational and registry-based, so they cannot prove causation and may be influenced by missing or inconsistently reported enrollment data.
paper_title: Language eligibility criteria and enrolled racial and ethnic composition in US clinical trials: a cross-sectional study
